title: Report agent spawn admission truth
description:
Objective: consume the start-admission contract from task-d4329e8d020f40308209397079c5004d so the orchestrator never reports SPAWNED when startup was refused and no child exists.

Deliverable: agent-wrapper awaits only startup admission (never child exit), returns a report with a distinguishable refusal outcome plus exact code/layer, records active work only for admitted children, and the wrapper main awaits that report before printing it. This replaces blocked task-58fd2c3781254d839ee27867f8f9f4e6, whose synchronous/no-contract-change rails were impossible against an exit-lifetime Promise.

NOT in scope: changing spawn validation/quoting or credential-write order, reimplementing agentSpawnInvocation, inventing codes for unknown exceptions, changing the wrapper verifier/poll interval, or waiting for an agent to exit before returning the staffing report.

Verification: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`; both legs are read separately and the daemon test output must show a nonzero executed count.
definitionOfDone: A real spawner preflight refusal driven through the wrapper returns a non-SPAWNED report that asserts `SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE` and `agent-spawn-invocation` literally; the test also proves the refusal came from the spawner layer, not an earlier wrapper guard.
An admitted start still reports the existing SPAWNED shape before its held-open exit promise settles, and existing success assertions remain intact after only the required async caller adaptation.
The wrapper/main wait only for startup admission and never for child exit; a held-open child test proves runOnce/reporting completes while the child remains active.
A refused start is never inserted into the active map and leaves activeCount at its exact prior value; an admitted start is inserted once and deleted in a finally path when its exit settles.
No rejection is blanket-swallowed: the typed refusal becomes a coded report, while any unclassified start failure rejects/fails closed rather than being logged or reported as SPAWNED.
Restoring the unconditional SPAWNED branch turns the named refusal code/layer test red; restore is byte-exact by SHA-256.
Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` passes under path-attributed baseline rules, and daemon Vitest output proves nonzero execution.
taskRails: Depends on task-d4329e8d020f40308209397079c5004d; do not mock or locally reimplement its start-admission contract if it is absent on disk.
The wrapper report must name both the stable code and refusing layer. `outcome !== SPAWNED` alone is not acceptance evidence.
Make runOnce/callers asynchronous only to await startup admission. Awaiting the child-exit promise would serialize the wrapper and is forbidden.
Do not touch agent-spawner production or tests in this consumer task; producer and consumer must remain independently reviewable.
Preserve the verifier and polling loop except for awaiting the truthful runOnce result, and commit only explicit owned paths.

TDD RED — and name the defect that makes today's tests unable to fail. `SpawnReport.outcome` is declared `"SPAWNED" | string` (agent-wrapper.ts:73-78). That `| string` collapses the union to `string`, so ANY value typechecks and any assertion comparing `outcome` to a refusal label passes whatever the code does. implementationPlan.description:
SWITCH THE CONSUMER TO THE ADMISSION-AWARE ENTRY. At `agent-wrapper-main.ts:253`, replace `claudeSpawner(mcpStarted.origin, {...})` with `claudeSpawnStarter(...)` and thread the returned `AgentSpawnStartResult` into the report built by `agent-wrapper.ts`. Keep the existing `onFatalContainment` wiring and the `secureSpawn = agentSpawner` assignment working; if the starter's type makes that assignment unsound, adjust the local type rather than casting — a cast here would re-hide the fact this task exists to surface.
THE ONE RULE THAT MATTERS: DO NOT AWAIT THE EXIT PROMISE. The `ok: true` arm carries `exit: Promise<void>`, which is the child's LIFETIME, not its admission. Awaiting it converts a fast admission report into a block for the whole run and silently reintroduces the defect in a new shape. The contract's `SpawnAttempt` type (agent-spawn-contract.ts:92) exists precisely to keep `admitted` and `done` separate — consume it. Attach a rejection handler to `exit` so an unhandled rejection cannot escape, but never `await` it on the reporting path.
On the refusal arm, propagate `code` and `layer` verbatim into the report. Do not re-wrap them into a wrapper-local code and do not stringify them into a message — both erase which layer refused, which is the whole content of "admission truth".

Typecheck could not see it — with a contextual return type of `Promise<AgentSpawnStartResult>`, `new Promise(() => undefined)` infers that type happily and simply never settles. Fixed by splitting the two facts in the injection: admission resolves, `exit` stays pending. A hang, not a wrong value, is what a missed adaptation looks like here.

One deliberate improvement rather than a mechanical fix — the `it.each` row named "rejected child exit" was `async () => { throw ... }`, which under the new contract is a rejected START, not a rejected exit. It now returns `{ok: true, exit: Promise.reject(...)}`, so the table again tests both halves it names: a start that was never admitted, and a start that WAS admitted and then died. Its assertions (settle rejects with the message, then `{active: 0, spawned: [], surfaceOutcome: failureMessage}`) are unchanged and green.

(1) Restore `| string` on the report's outcome type and confirm a NAMED refusal test goes red — or, if it stays GREEN, you have just proved the assertion was vacuous all along and the test must be strengthened before this task can complete. Record which. (2) Make the consumer discard the refusal arm and always report SPAWNED; the coded-refusal test must redden on the exact code AND layer, not merely on "not SPAWNED". (3) Make the consumer `await` the exit promise and confirm the admission-before-lifetime test reddens or times out visibly — proving that test actually pins the separation rather than passing because the child happened to exit fast. Bound that test so a regression reports a red rather than hanging. GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT — and the review found a defect MY OWN DIFF INTRODUCED, which I fixed and drilled before finishing.

THE ADVERSARIAL FINDING (concurrency, the checklist's first item). `runOnce` reads the affordance surface ONCE per pass, then loops the snapshot guarded by `active.size >= maxAgents` and `active.has(workItemId)`. While it was SYNCHRONOUS those guards were airtight — a pass ran to completion before anything could observe `active`. Adding `await staff(step)` turned them into check-then-act across a yield point: two overlapping passes read the same pre-staffing snapshot and can staff one item twice or overshoot maxAgents. Production's caller is a strictly sequential `for(;;) { await runOnce() }`, so nothing was broken today — but `runOnce` is exported and the hazard is created BY this diff, not inherited. Fixed with a 5-line pass-level latch (`pending.then(runPass, runPass)`, with `.catch` so a failed pass cannot poison the chain behind it). It serialises PASSES only — the pass still returns the moment admission resolves — so task rail 3 (never await a child lifetime) is untouched, and I say so explicitly because "serialise" is the word that rail uses about a different thing.
